mutant.description: The negative arm is the heart of this order, so it was controlled rather than asserted. (1) ISOLATING CONTROL: the probe parses not only {"mode":"rolling_complete_window","calendar_months":13} but the SAME scope WITHOUT calendar_months, which both packages must accept. Only if the prior accepts the plain scope and refuses the 13-month one is its refusal specific to calendar_months. That control FIRED THREE TIMES before the real read -- the first probe shaped `accounts` as a list and both packages refused on scope.accounts, the second refused on scope.columns -- and each time it correctly declined to call the negative arm satisfied, because a refusal was being produced by a malformed probe rather than by the defect. (2) The prior PACKAGE was downloaded before the act and its sha256 verified equal to the then-live CodeSha256, so the control is provably the bytes that were running. (3) A token census over each package's data_entitlement.py agrees from another direction: calendar_months appears 19 times in the deployed copy and 0 in the prior, which has no parse_rolling_window. (4) The CORRECTED AC2's own guard was controlled by running its command form against the bad name: it returns rc=0 with an EMPTY value through this device's aws shim, so the rc check alone would NOT have caught it -- the `[ -n "$live" ]` conjunct is what discriminates.
mutant.expected: The deployed package accepts the 13-month scope and carries the value; the prior refuses it while accepting the same scope without calendar_months; the live hash moves off the prior and equals the build.
mutant.observed: Deployed accepted with calendar_months=13 on the parsed Scope. Prior refused with Malformed 'a rolling_complete_window grant carries only its mode' and ACCEPTED the plain rolling scope, so refusal_is_specific_to_calendar_months is true. Live CodeSha256 moved ZyYCPPyP5CV.. -> 894RI63/G4h.., equal to the build and different from the prior. AC1 and AC2 both PASS where the issuer recorded them FAIL at base.
